tool.name: Make Design
tool.command:
@SHELL_OPTIONS@
#import re
## A design file is a table: the first line names the columns and its first cell is the ## word "group", every further line assigns one group of the source file to one set per ## grouping column. The sets of the first grouping form the default class, which is the ## one most commands work on. #set $rowtail = '' #for $grouping in $groupings: #if re.search('\s', str($grouping.name)): printf '[ERROR]: the name of a grouping must not contain whitespace: %s\n' '${grouping.name}' >&2 && exit 1 && #end if #set $rowtail += '\t' + str($grouping.name) #end for
## the groups of the source file: the second column of a group file (name and group) and ## of a shared file (label, group, number of OTUs, ...), whose first line is a header awk -F'\t' 'NR == 1 && $1 == "label" { next } { print $2 }' '$source' | sort -u > source_groups.txt &&
## every group of the source file has to be part of every grouping, otherwise the table ## has holes and the design file is unusable #for $i, $grouping in enumerate($groupings): #set $selection = ','.join([str($g) for $g in $grouping.groups]) printf '%s\n' '$selection' | tr ',' '\n' | sort -u > grouping_${i}.txt && comm -23 source_groups.txt grouping_${i}.txt > missing_${i}.txt && if [ -s missing_${i}.txt ]; then printf '[ERROR]: the grouping %s does not contain these groups of the source file:\n' '${grouping.name}' >&2 && sed 's/^/ /' missing_${i}.txt >&2 && exit 1; fi && #end for
printf 'group$rowtail\n' > design.txt && awk -v tail="$rowtail" '{ print $0 tail }' source_groups.txt >> design.txt && mv design.txt '$design'

param.name: source
param.label: Source containing groups
param.help: the design file gets one line per group of this file

param.name: name
param.label: Name for a new combined grouping
param.help: the name of the set column; it must not contain whitespace

param.name: groups
param.label: Select groups to include in this grouping

tool.help:
@MOTHUR_OVERVIEW@
**Command Documentation**
Make Design writes a design file, which assigns the groups of the source file to one or more sets per group. A design file is a table whose first line names the columns: the first column is called ``group`` and every further column is named after a grouping. Each line below the header holds the name of a group followed by the set it belongs to in each grouping. For the groups ``forest`` and ``pasture``, both in the grouping ``tardis``, the design file is::
group tardis forest tardis pasture tardis
Every group of the source file has to be part of every grouping, otherwise the table would have holes.
**Usage**
Design files are read by merge.groups_, indicator_ and metastats_. The sets of the first grouping column form the default class, which is the one most commands work on.
.. _merge.groups: https://mothur.org/wiki/merge.groups/ .. _indicator: https://mothur.org/wiki/indicator/ .. _metastats: https://mothur.org/wiki/metastats/
